meta.what: Round 6 revision of shadow_fleet.json (roadmap C3). Who controls the tankers carrying Russia's seaborne crude and oil-product exports, by country of the beneficial owner / commercial controller (not flag, not front-company registration), 2021-2026, split into the mainstream fleet (G7+-linked, KSE 'white') and the shadow fleet; and the resulting gross freight revenue per country. Russian-owned and Russian-controlled tankers count for no foreign country. Same structure as shadow_fleet.json; replaces it.
meta.units: Shares: fraction of the segment's barrels (crude, products, or crude+products weighted 58/42). freight: EUR bn GROSS freight revenue (not profit), nominal, ECB yearly average USD/EUR (2021 1.1827, 2022 1.0530, 2023 1.0813, 2024 1.0824, 2025 1.1300, 2026 1.1629 = same as shipping.json); 2026 = Jan-Aug, not annualised. Each value {low, central, high}, ~90% range. Ranges in round 6 come from a Monte Carlo (4,000 draws) over the Russian share of each manager bucket, the China west/Pacific split, the Greek shares, the freight pools and a residual allocation error per country (B 0.88-1.14, C 0.75-1.33, D 0.5-2.0); 5th-95th percentile.
meta.method: As round 5 (see shadow_fleet-notes.md) for the mainstream fleet, the shadow/white split and the freight pools. Changed: the shadow fleet is split by KSE monthly volume by country of ship/commercial manager into buckets, each with an evidence-based Russian-controlled share (low/central/high) and a nationality split of the non-Russian rest (bucket_table): Russia 100%; UAE 85/82/78/72/80% (2022-26; Sovcomflot chain 57-89% of named top-10 volume + Lukoil/Litasco and EU-listed Rosneft/Lukoil-linked Dubai firms); KSE 'China' split by loading region using KSE's Baltic chart - western shells (Baltic x1.25) 75% (50-90%), Pacific 20% (8-40%); India 60% (2022-23, Gatik/Rosneft) then 45%; Singapore 20%; Seychelles/Marshall Islands/Unknown 60% (2022) and 65% (2023-26), range 45-85% (was 50%, 25-80%); 'other' managers 33% named Russian fronts (20-45%) + 12% opaque. Cross-checks: KSE registered-owner chart (Russian-registered owners alone 45/36/26/19/17% of shadow volume 2022-26) is a lower bound; Ukraine's defence intelligence (HUR) estimate that Russia spent >USD 10bn buying shadow tankers since Dec 2022 is consistent with roughly half or more of the fleet's value being Russian-funded.

how_to_use: Replaces shadow_fleet.json (round 5) and the country allocation of FREIGHT in shipping.json (field countries.ISO3.freight and baseline_2019_2021 freight part). If the builder uses countries.ISO3.freight from this file: (a) do NOT also apply refine.json shipping_control freight_scale_vs_current_model (the Russian carve-out for UAE/IND/CHN/HKG is already inside these shares); (b) do NOT apply the 2026 freight x1.065 factor in apply_shipping (the 2026 crude pool here is already 11.0 instead of 9.7); (c) the insurance_finance items in shipping.json that follow owner shares can be scaled by freight_scale_vs_shipping_json; (d) ship_sales, registry and P&I-by-insurer parts of shipping.json are unchanged; (e) SYC, MHL get no freight here (fronts; their volume is split Russia/hubs), so the Seychelles 20% cut in fix_artefacts no longer matters for freight; (f) profit factors (SHIPPING_PROFIT freight 0.2/0.35/0.5) and overlap shares still apply on top - these are gross values. replacement_share_tables gives CRUDE and PRODUCTS share tables in the format of shipping.json's owner-share tables (RUS = Russian own and controlled pool).

ARE.reasoning: Round 6. (1) UAE-managed shadow volume (KSE: 12-18% of all seaborne barrels 2022-24, 10% 2025, 7% 2026) is 72-85% Russian-controlled (central): the Sovcomflot chain (Sun Ship, SCF Mgmt - OFAC: Sovcomflot property; Stream, Fornax, Avebury, Nova, Dreamer, Greenlight, Albatross, Lynx, Grace) is 57-89% of named top-10 UAE volume (refine.json), plus Lukoil's Litasco Middle East / Eiger Shipping (UK Jul 2025, EU Oct 2025) and Nova Shipmanagement / Citrine Marine, listed by the EU in Dec 2025 as linked to Rosneft/Lukoil. KSE registered-owner data agree: UAE-registered owners carry only 175-230 kb/d against 550-1,100 kb/d UAE-managed, while Russian-registered owners carry 550-950 kb/d with few Russian managers. Of the non-Russian rest, 55% is counted as UAE-resident control (the rest goes to Indian, Azerbaijani, Turkish and Chinese owners using Dubai companies). (2) 20% of the non-Russian part of opaque Seychelles/Marshall Islands/unknown owners and 25% of the non-Russian part of western 'China' shells (2Rivers-type Dubai networks). (3) UAE companies in the mainstream products trade (Onex DMCC). Certainty C.

AZE.reasoning: Round 6. Azerbaijani nationals behind Dubai/Hong Kong/Seychelles networks: the 2Rivers (ex-Coral Energy) group's shareholders and directors are Azerbaijani (UK sanctions May 2025, Feb 2026; EU Dec 2025), and at least 31 Azerbaijan-registered ISM companies manage sanctioned tankers (OCCRP Jun 2026). 2Rivers is counted mostly as Russian-controlled (Russian-bank financed, Rosneft-directed per the EU), so Azerbaijan only gets 35% of the non-Russian part of western 'China' shells, 10% of the non-Russian opaque and UAE-managed parts, and 8% of named 'other' managers. KSE shows Azerbaijan-registered owners at 160-260 kb/d (5-10% of shadow volume). Certainty D (who keeps the margin inside these networks is not public).

CHN.reasoning: Round 6. KSE 'China' managers (incl. Hong Kong) split by loading region using KSE's Baltic chart: Pacific part (Kozmino/De-Kastri to China; private owners such as Sunne, Prominent, Searun, Shang) is 20% Russian (8-40%), 55% of the rest mainland; the western part (Baltic plus an estimated 25% more at Black Sea/Arctic ports: 38-77% of 'China' volume) is 75% Russian (50-90%) because it is made up of serial single-ship Hong Kong/China shells (Windward Oct 2026: 45 tankers, one untraceable nominee, 40 with ISM managers in Sumqayit, earlier Seychelles/Marshall Islands SPVs, four ex-Litasco; KSE Baltic tables: Prizantal Shorelink, Krivet Shardline, Solvix League, Aetherion...), of which only 20% of the non-Russian part is mainland Chinese. Plus 22% of the non-Russian opaque remainder, IG-insured Chinese owners in the mainstream trade, and COSCO's share of Arc7 LNG (unchanged). Pacific shadow crude at 0.6x freight per barrel. Certainty C.

GRC.reasoning: Mainstream (G7+-linked, price-cap) fleet only. Greek beneficial owners' share of Russian seaborne barrels: crude 31% pre-war (Lloyd's List: a third of oil shipments Aug 2021), 40% in 2022 (LL: 50% of oil shipments Aug 2022, 42% of crude Oct 2022), 28% in 2023 (S&P: G7 tankers 52% of crude May 2023, Greeks 20%+ by Dec 2023), 13% in 2024 (S&P: Greek operators 11.5m bbl Jan, 16.6m bbl Feb 2024), 22% in 2025 (Kpler Jan-Jul 33% of crude; Windward 27% Jun, 16% Aug, <5% Nov after the EU cap cut), 9% in Jan-Aug 2026 (KSE top-10: Dynacom 3-6% of crude May-Aug, 2-5 Greek firms in the top 10). Products 28-38% throughout (Kpler 51% of fuel oil; Windward 43% of clean products Jun 2025; KSE: Greek firms hold 6-9 of the top-10 product shipper spots 2024-26). Cross-check: FT found USD 3.8bn for 389m priced barrels of crude Jul 2023-mid 2026 (scaled ~USD 1.8bn/yr); this model gives ~USD 1.65bn/yr for the same window. Greek-sold tankers now in the shadow fleet are NOT counted here (they are in shipping.json ship_sales).

HKG.reasoning: Round 6. 45% of the non-Russian Pacific 'China'-managed volume, 20% of the non-Russian western 'China' shells and 13% of the non-Russian opaque remainder. Sovcomflot itself uses Hong Kong shells as registered owners (Comitana, Insania, Vimena, Anchorstar, Glimmer Shipping HK: KSE Sep 2026 top-20 table), which count for Russia. Certainty C.

IND.reasoning: Round 6. India-managed shadow volume (KSE 1-8%): 60% Russian in 2022-23 (Gatik Ship Management: 58 tankers, >half of 83m bbl tracked by Kpler came from Rosneft, opaque owners, fleet moved to UAE/India affiliates), 45% from 2024 (Indian technical managers for Marshall Islands/Seychelles owners); 85% of the rest Indian. Plus 20% of the non-Russian UAE-managed part (Indian owners with Dubai companies), 20% of the non-Russian opaque remainder and IG-insured Indian owners in the mainstream trade. Certainty C.

russia_own_and_controlled.note: Sovcomflot and its UAE/Hong Kong/Omani fronts, Russian-registered managers (South Fleet, Invest Fleet, Idas, SCF TM), Lukoil (Litasco/Eiger) and Rosneft-directed networks (2Rivers counted 2/3 Russian via the opaque and western 'China' buckets), Russian owners still IG-insured before the Dec 2022 bans, and the Russian share of opaque Seychelles/Marshall Islands/unknown owners. Counts for Russia itself, not for any foreign country.

overlaps: This file (round 6) replaces shadow_fleet.json (round 5) one for one; it is a re-allocation of the freight part of shipping.json, not a new flow: use it INSTEAD of shipping.json freight (and instead of refine.json shipping_control scaling and the 2026 x1.065 factor), never in addition. Totals are close: all-foreign gross freight 2022-26 here vs shipping.json are given in totals; the difference is mostly the 2026 crude pool (11.0 vs 9.7 USD bn) and a larger Russian pool than shipping.json had before refine. Ship sales (Greek and other tankers sold into the shadow fleet) stay in shipping.json ship_sales and are not in these shares, so a Greek-built/ex-Greek tanker now run by a UAE front counts here for the controller (often Russia) and its sale premium counts for the seller in ship_sales - no double count. Services overlap (uncovered.json sold_to_rus) and CIF overlap with fossil-fuel payments are unchanged and handled by shipping.json overlap_share_with_services_sold_to_rus, which still applies per country. uncovered.json GRC.oil_shipping_earned remains replaced by shipping.json. Insurance by insurer country (UK, Norway IG clubs vs Ingosstrakh) is not re-estimated here. Round 6 adds no new flow: only the split of the same freight pools between Russia and foreign controllers changes. The Azerbaijan freight here (2Rivers-type networks) is shipping freight, not oil trading margin; trading margins of hub traders are in hub_buyers.json / laundered-oil files and are not touched. Ship sales to these networks stay in shipping.json ship_sales.
notes: Gross freight, not profit. Biggest remaining guesses: the Russian share of opaque Seychelles/Marshall Islands/unknown owners (now 65%, 45-85%, from network evidence; no vessel-level beneficial-owner dataset was reachable), how much of the 2Rivers network's margin stays with its Azerbaijani/Dubai owners (counted 1/3 foreign), the Black Sea/Arctic part of 'China'-managed shells (25% of the Baltic amount, 0-60%), and the nationality split of non-Russian Dubai companies. Lloyd's List Intelligence / S&P beneficial-owner fields per vessel would settle most of this.
